page: Microsoft Azure M128-32ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized server running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor configuration includes a 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 38 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA.

This instance is equipped with 3892.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 121.62 GB of RAM per physical core. It includes 4194 GB of local storage and supports premium storage capabilities. No GPUs are bundled with this configuration, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core metrics achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests show average read performance, but large-block write memory bandwidth is strong, placing in the top 25% of tested systems.

Given the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong write memory bandwidth, the M128-32ms is designed for memory-intensive workloads rather than raw compute-bound tasks. It is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and enterprise database operations. While the high-end memory allocation represents a significant resource investment, the lower single-core performance suggests it is less efficient for single-threaded processing or compute-heavy workloads like LLM text generation.
